summary: Three additive spec capabilities driven by UC6 (Flood Warning System, EA -> Leidos): symmetric (passphrase) PGP on both the ingest and egress sides, gzip as a landing-member container, and a configurable CSV dialect plus gzip archive format on the pgp_zip sink. Plus two JSON-schema-only fixes. NOTHING IS REMOVED and every default preserves pre-1.7.4 behaviour, so no existing spec changes shape or needs migrating.

added_attributes.description: The landing archive's CONTAINER, orthogonal to any decryption layer. 'zip' is a real archive with N named members, opened by pyzipper. 'gzip' is a single compressed stream with no member table, which pyzipper cannot open at all.
added_attributes.ui_action: Add a select to the ZIP-handling section, labelled 'Archive container', options zip (default) / gzip. Show a hint under 'gzip': 'An UNENCRYPTED .gz needs no ZIP handling at all -- Spark decompresses it on read. Use gzip only for an encrypted .gz (e.g. .csv.gz.gpg).'
added_attributes.validation: Reject any other value. When 'gzip', reject pre_extraction_decryption.secret_passphrase.
added_attributes.migration: None -- absent means 'zip', the only pre-1.7.4 behaviour.

added_attributes.description: 'pgp_symmetric' decrypts a passphrase-encrypted OpenPGP message -- the shape `gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256` produces. Kept as a distinct type rather than an optional extra secret on 'pgp' because the two are mutually exclusive at the message level: a key-encrypted message is not passphrase-decryptable and vice versa.
added_attributes.ui_action: Add 'pgp_symmetric' to the decryption-type select. When selected, HIDE private_key_secret and make passphrase_secret REQUIRED. When 'pgp' is selected, keep today's behaviour (private_key_secret required, passphrase_secret optional).
added_attributes.validation: type 'pgp_symmetric' REQUIRES passphrase_secret and REJECTS private_key_secret.
added_attributes.rejection_message_verbatim: source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_extraction_decryption.private_key_secret: not valid for type 'pgp_symmetric' -- a passphrase-encrypted OpenPGP message has no recipient keypair. Use type 'pgp' for a key-encrypted message.

added_attributes.description: The staged CSV's dialect. Before 1.7.4 the writer used Python's csv `excel` default -- comma-separated, always headered, CRLF-terminated -- with no way to express a supplier interface that specifies otherwise.
added_attributes.ui_action: Add a collapsible 'CSV format' group under the sink editor, shown ONLY when format is pgp_zip and staged_file_format is csv. Three controls: a single-character text input (delimiter), a checkbox (include_header), and a select crlf/lf (line_terminator). line_terminator is spelled as a name because JSON cannot carry a bare control character.
added_attributes.validation: Reject when staged_file_format != 'csv'; reject a multi-character delimiter; reject a line_terminator outside {crlf, lf}.
added_attributes.rejection_message_verbatim: target_config.sink_config.staged_file_options.delimiter: must be exactly one character, got '||' -- Python's csv writer cannot emit a multi-character delimiter.
added_attributes.migration: None -- omitting the object reproduces the pre-1.7.4 dialect exactly.

added_attributes.description: The finished export's container. 'gzip' concatenates this micro-batch's staged partition files into ONE gzip stream (a gzip holds exactly one member) and names the export '<export_file_name_format>.<csv|jsonl>.gz', or '....gz.gpg' when pgp_encryption is on. The per-file CSV header is emitted per partition, so all but the first are dropped on concatenation.
added_attributes.ui_action: Add a select 'Archive format' to the export section: zip (default) / gzip. When gzip is selected, DISABLE the 'secret' (AES ZIP password) field with the hint 'A gzip stream has no archive password.' and update the filename preview to <stem>.csv.gz[.gpg].

added_attributes.description: Symmetric (passphrase) egress encryption. Exactly one of passphrase_secret or recipient_public_key_secret must be set when pgp_encryption.enabled is true. Before 1.7.4 the recipient key was unconditionally required, so symmetric encryption was unreachable from a spec.
added_attributes.ui_action: In the PGP-encryption section add a radio: 'Encrypt to a recipient key' (today's behaviour) vs 'Encrypt with a shared passphrase'. Passphrase mode shows ONE secret picker and HIDES recipient_public_key_secret, sign_with_private_key_secret and sign_passphrase_secret -- signing needs a sender keypair and is unavailable here.
added_attributes.validation: Reject when both secrets are present; reject when neither is and enabled is true; reject signing fields alongside passphrase_secret.
added_attributes.rejection_message_verbatim: target_config.sink_config.post_export_archive.pgp_encryption: 'passphrase_secret' (symmetric) and 'recipient_public_key_secret' (asymmetric) are mutually exclusive -- set exactly one.
added_attributes.migration: None -- existing recipient-key specs are unchanged.

modified_attributes.after: Required only when passphrase_secret is absent (exactly-one-of).
modified_attributes.ui_action: Drive the required flag from the encryption-mode radio above, not from `enabled`.
modified_attributes.migration: None -- a spec that sets it keeps working unchanged.

modified_attributes.before: Accepted by the Python validator (in ALLOWED_TRANSFORMATION_FLOW_KEYS) but ABSENT from the JSON schema, whose additionalProperties:false rejected it -- so a spec setting it passed validate_spec and was then refused at onboarding.
modified_attributes.after: Declared in the schema; both gates now agree.
modified_attributes.ui_action: The description field may now be shown for transformation flows as well as ingestion flows. It becomes the target table's Unity Catalog COMMENT.

modified_attributes.before: reconciliationTargetConfig composes reconciliationDatasetConfig via allOf; the base def set additionalProperties:false, which cannot see sibling-branch properties, so target_id / comparison_direction / append_target_table were always rejected. EVERY reconciliation spec in flowx_testing/ failed the schema.
modified_attributes.after: Closed with unevaluatedProperties at the composed level, which evaluates across allOf branches. Unknown keys are still rejected.
modified_attributes.ui_action: None functionally. If the app previously worked around this by skipping schema validation for reconciliation target configs, that workaround can be removed.

app_update_checklist: databricks-app/config/registry/*.json -- add the 5 new attributes with their types, defaults, enums and applies_when conditions.
databricks-app/config/attribute_knowledge*.json -- add the descriptions verbatim from this file; they explain WHY each attribute exists, which is what the assistant surfaces.

databricks-app/config/validation/rules.json -- add the exactly-one-of rule for pgp_encryption, the single-character delimiter rule, the two enum rules, and the member_format 'gzip' vs secret_passphrase conflict.

databricks-app/web/src/registry.js and Builder.jsx -- render the conditional groups described in each ui_action. Anchor edits on exact line prefixes; never a broad regex (a DOTALL re.sub once swallowed ~650 lines of Builder.jsx). Run `node --check` after.
databricks-app/server/settings.py -- no change expected; confirm explicitly rather than assuming.
npm run build in databricks-app/web -- REQUIRED. Databricks Apps does not build at deploy time, so an un-rebuilt web/dist/ keeps serving the old form.
Deploy is TWO steps: `bundle deploy` then `bundle run` -- deploy alone leaves the app on its previous code.

verification.regression_check: Full tests/unit diffed by failing-test-ID against a pre-change baseline: 125 vs 127. Zero regressions; two pre-existing resource-layout failures fixed. Counts alone are unreliable in this repo (the offline baseline swings widely), so the ID sets were compared.
verification.bundle_validate: databricks bundle validate -t dev_flowx --var=wheels_root=... -> Validation OK!
verification.external_interop: Symmetric PGP round-tripped against the real GnuPG 2.4.9 CLI in BOTH directions with a gzip payload: the framework decrypts what gpg wrote, and gpg decrypts what the framework wrote.
